body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「你要從三個會更新的 upstream feed 組一個本地 review queue。每個 feed 都有 cursor，record 會遲到、同一秒更新，亦可能重送。你點樣交出最新一百條而唔漏、唔重複，並且 crash 後可以續跑？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「我會按 timestamp sort，儲低最後一個 page number 或 timestamp，下次由嗰度繼續。」

Timestamp 同 page number 都未必代表一個穩定位置。兩個 record 可以同一秒出現；upstream 可能在你翻頁時插入新 record；page number 會因為新資料而移位；而「最新」亦未講清楚是 source publish time、event time，還是本地收到的時間。Cursor 只是某一個 source 交畀你嘅繼續讀取位置，不是跨三個 source 的全域排序保證。

## 先定義你想保持甚麼順序

先寫一條排序 contract。若業務只需要把合成 review items 按事件時間展示，可用 `(event_time, source_id, record_id)` 作 stable key；同一個 timestamp 時用 source ID 和 immutable record ID 打破平手。若 record 可被更正，還要定義 version：是把最新 version 取代舊 version，還是保留修訂事件？這不是 sorting 的小細節，而是使用者看到兩個互相矛盾版本時系統要做甚麼。

每個 source 的 cursor 要原樣保存，連同 source snapshot 或 fetch time、response hash／receipt 和 schema version。不要把 opaque cursor 當數字加一。從多個已排序的 source 取第一百條時，可用一個大小約等於 source 數目的 min-heap 做 k-way merge：每個 source 暫時放一條候選，取最早／最新一條後才向同一 source 拉下一條。三個 source 不需要把所有 record 載入 memory 才能排序。

## Resume 不是只記最後一個 timestamp

Checkpoint 最少要有 run ID、每個 source 的 cursor、已接受 record 的 immutable ID 和 version、最後輸出的 composite key，以及本次採用的 ordering policy version。Crash 後先重讀一段可重疊的 window，再用 ID 加 version 去 deduplicate；不要假定網絡 timeout 前的 response 完全沒落地。這是 at-least-once intake 的常見做法：允許多看一次，靠明確 key 防止同一個結果被重複交畀 reviewer。

Late arrival 亦需要一條公開規則。你可以保留一段 watermark window，定期重算最近十分鐘；也可以把比已發出 queue 更舊的新 item 放進「late review」lane，而不是偷偷插到已交付的第一頁。選哪一種取決於 reviewer 是否需要穩定頁面、錯過新資料的代價、以及誰決定重播。

## 三個書籤，不是一個總次序

想像三間圖書館各自排好新書車。Cursor 是每間圖書館給你的書籤，告訴你下次由哪裏繼續看；它不會替三間圖書館排出共同的第一名。你要自己訂「新書」的日期規則、同日的次序，以及同一本書後來有修訂，應該取代舊版定保留兩個版本。停電後，重新看一小段書架，再核對書號，才不會重複借出同一本。

## 面試時要講到的決定

可以這樣答：「我不會用 page number 當 checkpoint。我會為每個 source 保留 opaque cursor 和 receipt，定義跨 source 的 composite ordering key，再用 bounded k-way merge 逐條取候選。Checkpoint 保存 source cursor、last emitted key、record ID／version 和 policy version。重啟時重播一個小 window、去重後再輸出。對遲到資料，我會選明文 watermark 或 late lane，並量度 duplicate rate、late-arrival rate、queue churn 和 source lag。」

AI Engineer 需要識得分辨演算法保證和產品承諾。Heap 幫你有效率地 merge；cursor 幫你續讀一個 source；但「reviewer 今日見到甚麼」是資料定義、政策和恢復設計共同決定的。

## 別只講 sort 和 pagination

「我會 sort by timestamp」太薄。要追問：timestamp 是由誰產生？clock skew 怎麼辦？來源更新同新建可否同時出現？同一 record 重送但 payload 不同怎麼辦？cursor 過期時是否需要 full reconciliation？第一百條交給 reviewer 後，較早到達的 record 可不可以插進原頁？

用 fixed fixtures 測：相同 timestamp、跨 source duplicate、late arrival、更新後 version changed、cursor 過期、source timeout、在 checkpoint 與寫出之間 crash。每個 fixture 都要有 source receipt、expected order 和 expected route，避免測試只剩一個漂亮的 merged list。

## 可以留下的工程證據

- `ordering-contract.md`：時間欄位、composite key、version rule、late-data policy 和 non-goal。
- `source-receipt.schema.json`：source URL／ID、opaque cursor、fetch time、snapshot reference 和 schema version。
- `merge.ts`：bounded k-way merge，不會一次讀盡所有 source。
- `checkpoint.json`：cursor、last emitted key、record version 和 run ID 的示例。
- `merge-recovery.test.ts`：同時 timestamp、重送、遲到、cursor expiry 和 crash fixture。

## 延伸閱讀

[公開資料要有 source receipt](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-public-dataset-needs-a-source-receipt)、[Retry 成功，點解 workflow 仍然可以出事？](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan)，以及 [Priority queue 為何需要 stale-entry rule](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-priority-queue-needs-a-staleness-rule)。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。feeds、cursors、records、timestamps、watermark、queue 和 artefact 都是 synthetic 教學材料；它不代表任何平台的 pagination contract、資料完整性承諾或真實面試流程。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “You are building a local review queue from three upstream feeds that change while you read them. Each feed has a cursor; records can arrive late, share a timestamp, or be resent. How do you return the newest hundred without gaps or duplicates, and resume after a crash?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would sort by timestamp and persist the last page number or timestamp.”

A timestamp and a page number do not necessarily identify a stable position. Two records can appear in the same second; an upstream service can insert new records while you paginate; page numbers move as data arrives; and “newest” might mean publish time, event time, or the time your service received a record. A cursor is one source's continuation token. It is not a global ordering guarantee across three sources.

## Define the order you are trying to preserve

Write an ordering contract first. If the work is to display synthetic review items by event time, `(event_time, source_id, record_id)` can be a stable composite key: source ID and immutable record ID break timestamp ties. If a record can be corrected, define the version rule too. Does a newer version replace the older one, or do you retain revision events? That is not a sorting footnote; it determines what the reviewer sees when two versions disagree.

Preserve each source cursor exactly as received, together with a source snapshot or fetch time, response hash or receipt, and schema version. Never increment an opaque cursor as though it were a number. To take the first hundred from several sorted sources, use a min-heap roughly the size of the source count for a k-way merge. Keep one candidate from each source; after taking the next item, fetch the next candidate only from that same source. Three feeds do not require loading every record into memory before ordering.

## Resume is more than the last timestamp

A checkpoint needs at least a run ID, every source cursor, the immutable ID and version of accepted records, the last emitted composite key, and the ordering-policy version. After a crash, reread a small overlapping window and deduplicate by ID plus version. Do not assume that a response lost to a network timeout never reached your process. This is a common at-least-once intake pattern: tolerate seeing a record again, then prevent the same result from reaching a reviewer twice with an explicit key.

Late arrivals also need a stated rule. You might keep a watermark window and recompute the most recent ten minutes, or place a newly discovered but older item in a `late-review` lane rather than silently inserting it into a page already delivered. The choice depends on whether reviewers need stable pages, the cost of missing new information, and who decides to replay work.

## Three bookmarks are not one global order

Imagine three libraries, each with its own trolley of new books. A cursor is a bookmark from one library, telling you where to continue there. It cannot rank the three libraries together. You must define what date makes a book “new,” the order for the same date, and whether a later revision should replace the earlier one or both versions should remain. After a power cut, look again at a small stretch of shelves and check book IDs before lending anything twice.

## The decision an interviewer is listening for

A useful answer is: “I would not use a page number as a checkpoint. I retain each source's opaque cursor and receipt, define a cross-source composite key, and take candidates with a bounded k-way merge. The checkpoint stores source cursors, last emitted key, record ID/version, and policy version. On restart I replay a short window, deduplicate, then emit. For late data I choose an explicit watermark or late lane, and measure duplicate rate, late-arrival rate, queue churn, and source lag.”

An AI Engineer needs to distinguish an algorithmic guarantee from a product promise. A heap merges efficiently; a cursor continues one source; but what a reviewer sees today is decided jointly by data definitions, policy, and recovery design.

## Where an answer goes thin

“I sort by timestamp” is too thin. Ask: Who creates the timestamp? What about clock skew? Can an update and a new record appear together? What if the same record is resent with different content? Does an expired cursor require reconciliation? Once the hundred records are delivered, may an earlier-arriving record be inserted into that same page?

Test fixed fixtures for equal timestamps, cross-source duplicates, late arrivals, changed versions, expired cursors, source timeouts, and a crash between checkpoint and output. Every fixture needs a source receipt, expected order, and expected route, not only a polished merged list.

## Engineering artefacts to leave behind

- `ordering-contract.md`: time field, composite key, version rule, late-data policy, and non-goal.
- `source-receipt.schema.json`: source URL or ID, opaque cursor, fetch time, snapshot reference, and schema version.
- `merge.ts`: bounded k-way merge that does not load every source at once.
- `checkpoint.json`: example cursor, last emitted key, record version, and run ID.
- `merge-recovery.test.ts`: equal-timestamp, resend, late-arrival, cursor-expiry, and crash fixtures.

## Further reading

[A public dataset needs a source receipt](/en/interview-lab/a-public-dataset-needs-a-source-receipt), [a retry is not a recovery plan](/en/interview-lab/a-retry-is-not-a-recovery-plan), and [why a priority queue needs a staleness rule](/en/interview-lab/a-priority-queue-needs-a-staleness-rule).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question exercise. The feeds, cursors, records, timestamps, watermark, queue, and artefacts are synthetic teaching material; they do not describe any platform's pagination contract, data-completeness promise, or interview process.
